newsitem.title: FRANCE: French water reserves situation remains worrying.
newsitem.headline: French water reserves situation remains worrying.

text.p: Rain in May only partly refilled depleted ground water reserves in France following a prolonged spring drought and the situation remains "worrying", the farm ministry said on Wednesday.

"May rain only partly restored ground water reserves that were experiencing a sharp shortfall across the territory and notably in the southern part following particularly dry weather in March and April," the ministry said in its latest report on crop conditions.
"Overall the situation of water reserves remains worrying, due to a lack of rain in March and April," it added.
May rainfall was around normal levels for the month in the Northeast and Centre east and above normal in the west and southwest.
But precipitation were 70 percent below normal in the Southeast and 30 percent below normal in the Corsica island.
The rain helped winter grain crops partly maintain their potential north of the Loire river but the situation looks worse in the south.
Rain and warmer temperatures were favourable to the development of spring crops though showers delayed some sowings.
In its first estimate for the 1997 harvest the ministry predicted winter barley and rapeseed production would fall as dry weather in March and April hit yields.
